title: What the prophets foretold was worthy of God
source_text: Ἀληθεύει οὖν ἐν μόνῳ κατὰ τὸν τόπον ὁ Κέλσος τῷ· ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἂν προείποιεν τοῦτο οἱ προφῆται· κακὸν γάρ ἐστι καὶ ἀνόσιον. τί δὲ τοῦτο ἢ ὅτι ὁ μέγας θεὸς δουλεύσει ἢ τεθνήξεται; ἄξιον δὲ θεοῦ τὸ προφητευθέν ἐστιν ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν, ὅτι τῆς θείας φύσεως „ἀπαύγασμα“ καὶ „χαρακτήρ“ τις ἐνανθρωπούσῃ ψυχῇ ἱερᾷ τῇ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ συνεπιδημήσει τῷ βίῳ, ἵνα σπείρῃ λόγον, οἰκειοῦντα τῷ τῶν ὅλων θεῷ τὸν παραδεξάμενον αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν καὶ γεωργήσαντα καὶ ἐπὶ τέλος ἀγαγόντα πάντα, ὃς τὴν δύναμιν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔχει τοῦ ἐν ἀνθρώπου σώματι καὶ ψυχῇ ἐσομένου θεοῦ λόγου. οὕτως δ᾿ ἔσται, ὡς μὴ ἀποκεκλεῖσθαι τὰς αὐγὰς αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐκείνῳ μόνῳ μηδ᾿ ὀνομάζεσθαι ὅτι οὐδαμοῦ ἀλλαχοῦ ἐστι τὸ τῶν αὐγῶν τούτων παρεκτικὸν φῶς, θεὸς λόγος ὤν. τὰ περὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν τοίνυν καθὸ μὲν νενόηται θεότητι ἐν αὐτῷ πραχθέντα, ἐστὶν ὅσια, καὶ οὐ μαχόμενα τῇ περὶ τοῦ θείου ἐννοίᾳ· καθὸ δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἦν, παντὸς μᾶλλον ἀνθρώπου κεκοσμημένος τῇ ἄκρᾳ μετοχῇ τοῦ αὐτολόγου καὶ τῆς αὐτοσοφίας ὑπέμεινεν ὡς σοφὸς καὶ τέλειος ἅπερ ἐχρῆν ὑπομεῖναι τὸν ὑπὲρ παντὸς τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἢ καὶ τῶν λογικῶν πάντα πράττοντα. καὶ οὐδὲν ἄτοπον καὶ ἀποτεθνηκέναι τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ οὐ μόνον παράδειγμα ἐκκεῖσθαι τοῦ ὑπὲρ εὐσεβείας ἀποθνῄ σκειν ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ εἰργάσθαι ἀρχὴν καὶ προκοπὴν τῆς καταλύσεως τοῦ πονηροῦ καὶ διαβόλου, πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν νενεμημένου. σημεῖα δὲ τῆς καθαιρέσεώς εἰσιν αὐτοῦ οἱ διὰ τὴν ἐπιδημίαν Ἰησοῦ πανταχόθεν φυγόντες μὲν τοὺς κατέχοντας αὐτοὺς δαίμονας, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἠλευθερῶσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς ὑπ᾿ ἐκείνους δουλείας ἀνατιθέντες ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῇ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῖς καθαρωτέρᾳ ὁσημέραι εἰς αὐτὸν εὐσεβείᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: Celsus therefore speaks truth (ἀληθεύω) in only one thing in the passage (τόπος): 'but the prophets would not foretell this; for it is evil and unholy.' But what is this, other than that the great God will be a slave or will die? But worthy of God is the thing prophesied by the prophets, that a 'radiance (ἀπαύγασμα)' and 'stamp (χαρακτήρ)' of the divine nature (θεία φύσις) will sojourn together (συνεπιδημέω) in life (βίος) with the holy (ἱερός) soul of Jesus becoming man (ἐνανθρωπέω), that it may sow (σπείρω) a word (λόγος) making kin (οἰκειόω) to the God of the wholes (ὁ τῶν ὅλων θεός) the one who received it into his own soul and cultivated (γεωργέω) and led (ἄγω) all to the end (τέλος), [a word] which has in itself the power (δύναμις) of God the Word who will be in a man's body and soul. And so it will be, that its rays (αὐγαί) are not shut up (ἀποκλείω) in that one alone, nor is it named that nowhere else is the light (φῶς) supplying (παρεκτικός) these rays, being God the Word. The things about Jesus therefore, in so far as they have been understood (νοέω) as done by Godhead (θεότης) in him, are holy and not fighting (μάχομαι) against the notion (ἔννοια) about the divine; but in so far as he was a man, adorned (κοσμέω) more than every man with the highest participation (μετοχή) of the Self-Word (αὐτόλογος) and Self-Wisdom (αὐτοσοφία), he endured (ὑπομένω), as wise and perfect (τέλειος), the things which one doing all things on behalf of the whole race (γένος) of men, or even of rational beings (λογικοί), had to endure. And nothing absurd both that the man has died, and his death is set forth (ἔκκειμαι) not only as an example (παράδειγμα) of dying for godliness (εὐσέβεια), but also has worked (ἐργάζομαι) a beginning (ἀρχή) and progress (προκοπή) of the dissolution (κατάλυσις) of the evil one and devil (διάβολος), who had distributed / held (νέμω, perf. mid.) the whole earth. Signs (σημεῖα) of his overthrow (καθαίρεσις) are those who through the sojourn (ἐπιδημία) of Jesus from everywhere have fled (φεύγω) the demons (δαίμονες) holding (κατέχω) them, and through having been freed (ἐλευθερόω) from the slavery (δουλεία) under them dedicate (ἀνατίθημι) themselves to God and to the godliness toward him, purer (καθαρός) daily (ὁσημέραι) as far as possible for them.
pass_b_english: In this passage, then, Celsus speaks the truth on one point only: “But the prophets would not foretell this, for it is evil and unholy.” And what is “this” but that the great God will be a slave or will die? What the prophets prophesied is worthy of God: that a certain “radiance” and “imprint” (Hebrews 1:3) of the divine nature would come to dwell in this life together with the holy soul of Jesus as it became man, in order to sow a word that makes kin to the God of the universe the one who receives it into his own soul, tends it, and brings it all to completion. That word holds in itself the power of God the Word, who was to be in a human body and soul. Yet it will be in such a way that his rays are not shut up in him alone, and it is not said that the light which gives these rays, being God the Word, is nowhere else.

The things concerning Jesus, then, in so far as they are understood to have been done by the Godhead in him, are holy and do not conflict with the notion of the divine. But in so far as he was a man, adorned more than any other man by the highest share in the very Word and the very Wisdom, he endured, as one wise and perfect, what had to be endured by one who does all things on behalf of the whole human race, or even of rational beings.

And there is nothing absurd in the man’s having died, and in his death not only standing as an example of dying for the sake of godliness, but also having brought about the beginning and the advance of the destruction of the evil one, the devil, who had held the whole earth as his domain. The signs of his overthrow are those who, through the coming of Jesus, have everywhere escaped the demons that held them, and who, having been freed from slavery under them, devote themselves to God and to a godliness toward him that grows purer day by day, as far as they are able.

choices.choice: ἀπαύγασμα and χαρακτήρ are from Hebrews 1:3 (radiance of his glory, imprint of his nature); cited inline. τις is kept (‘a certain’), and χαρακτήρ is rendered ‘imprint’ without an added ‘exact’. The sowing of the word may echo the parable of the sower (Matthew 13:3-23; Luke 8:11), but Origen does not quote it, so it is left uncited. The devil holding the whole earth may echo 1 John 5:19; too loose to cite. τοῦ πονηροῦ καὶ διαβόλου rendered ‘the evil one, the devil’ (one figure). πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν νενεμημένου is ambiguous (νέμω: to hold as one’s portion, to range over); rendered ‘who had held the whole earth as his domain’. αὐτόλογος and αὐτοσοφία rendered ‘the very Word’ and ‘the very Wisdom’. κατάλυσις rendered ‘destruction’ and καθαίρεσις ‘overthrow’ to keep the two words apart. καθὸ μὲν νενόηται θεότητι ἐν αὐτῷ πραχθέντα: dative θεότητι taken as agent (‘done by the Godhead in him’). The first sentence echoes Celsus’s words from 7.14.
restored τις ('a certain') and dropped the added 'exact' before 'imprint' (χαρακτήρ)
ἐν ἐκείνῳ μόνῳ: 'in that one man alone' -> 'in him alone' ('man' was added)
τῇ περὶ τοῦ θείου ἐννοίᾳ: dropped the added 'our' ('the notion of the divine')
αὐτόλογος / αὐτοσοφία made parallel: 'the very Word and the very Wisdom'
'what he had to endure who does all things' (stiff) -> 'what had to be endured by one who does all things'; dropped the added 'all' before 'rational beings'
ἐκκεῖσθαι ... εἰργάσθαι are parallel infinitives: 'being set forth ... as having brought about' -> 'standing as an example ... but also having brought about'
κατάλυσις 'overthrow' -> 'destruction', so it is not merged with καθαίρεσις ('overthrow')
διὰ τοῦ ἠλευθερῶσθαι: 'being freed' -> 'having been freed'
Scripture checked: Hebrews 1:3 (ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως) confirmed; Celsus's repeated words from 7.14 in double quotes
